prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No AI storyteller has been shown to grow toddlers' vocabulary, so the Main KPI of 150,000,000 toddlers with an AI storytelling companion is unmet in its intended sense. The controlled evidence covers older children only: an RCT of 67 children aged 5 to 8 learning English found LLM-guided dialogic reading gave vocabulary gains comparable to parent-led reading (https://doi.org/10.1111/bjet.13615), and Mathemyths found 35 children aged 4 to 8 learned mathematical language comparably with an LLM or a human storytelling partner (https://doi.org/10.1145/3613904.3642647). For under-threes, the proven route is human: a global meta-analysis of parenting interventions in the first three years shows gains in child development (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/33970913), and reviews of screen exposure in young children raise cognitive concerns (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/36059724). Open-source AI storyteller apps exist on GitHub (TaleWeaver for ages 4 to 10, GabbyGarden) with no outcome evaluation. Class neutral: potential language benefit, but real risk for under-threes from screen and AI exposure, data collection and displacing caregiver talk. Honest limit: building an LLM storyteller is a known answer and is not new work; the open, checkable work is a safe, voice-first, play-based design for children under three with a measured vocabulary effect against caregiver-led reading.
